author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Greens to Announce Plan for ‘Emergency Brake’ on Rent Hikes
content:
Green party leader Zack Polanski will set out plans for a three-year emergency brake on rent hikes to give renters “breathing space”.




The move would limit rises to whichever is lowest between Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation, wage growth or 2% – echoing existing metrics for pensions, which currently increase by the highest of either inflation, wage growth or 2.5%.




Under the proposal, landlords would not be able to put up rents by more than the lowest of the three measures, which the Greens say would protect tenants from being forced out by sudden rent hikes.




Addressing delegates at the Green party conference in Brighton on Friday, Polanski will also set out plans for a “fair rents guarantee” that would keep rents “fair and affordable” once the emergency brake expires after three years.




The party says the temporary cap would give wages time to catch up with rents, which have risen faster than incomes.




“For too long, landlords have been able to hike prices way beyond wages,” Polanski is expected to say.




“That’s why today I’m calling for a three-year emergency brake on private rents. No rent rises above CPI, wage growth or 2% – whichever is lower. No sudden hikes. No evictions under the guise of rent rises. No more fear and uncertainty.”

author: Ash Sarkar
title: Early Release of Prisoners Could Land Andy Burnham in the Slammer
content:
The early release scheme 

kicked into action

 yesterday, with the first batch of prisoners being released after serving 40% of their sentence or more. Hundreds of prisoners across England and Wales, whose sentences were up to 19 months, were let out early. Have Andy Burnham and his cabinet have become radical prison abolitionists?




Not quite. Labour were bounced into it by the 

dangerously overcrowded

 prisons system: a result of the Conservative government being keen to jail more people, but reluctant to build more prisons. The scheme will progress 

through phases

 into the summer of next year, when by June inmates serving more than 12 years will be eligible for release.




The previous Labour government had little choice but to introduce legislation designed to alleviate pressure on prison cells. This past summer, the 

adult male prisons estate

 was running at 98% capacity – putting us at one IKEA riot away from system collapse (

real ones will remember

). But the road to early release had some bumps along the way.




Newly-minted Prime Minister Burnham found himself in hot water when it emerged that the young men convicted of killing PC Harper in 2019, when he was dragged by a car as they fled the scene of a theft, would be eligible for early release. One million people 

signed a petition

 demanding they remain incarcerated; Andrew Harper’s widow made high-p

author: Novara Media
title: Tories & Lib Dems Scramble for Response to Burnham Speech
content:
Andy Burnham’s announcement of a triple lock shakeup has plunged Britain’s competing parties into chaos.




Plus: Another botched execution in the US reopens the death penalty discourse, and Andy Burnham’s wild decision to back Manchester City amid one of the biggest football controversies of all time.




With NoJusticeMTG, Dalia Gebrial, Maya Foa & Jan Zglinski.

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Spain’s Tenants’ Rights Protesters Win Reforms After 87-Year-Old Evicted
content:
Spain’s government has approved new measures to support tenants’ rights following widespread protests – but they need approval from congress and campaigners say they do not go far enough. 




Around 30,000 people marched through Madrid on Saturday, and 

hundreds remained for days

 in encampments across the capital’s central plazas, after an 87-year-old woman was forcibly removed from her home of 70 years on a stretcher. 




Maricarmen Abascal was evicted after her rent rose from €500 (£428) to €1,650 

and she was unable to pay

. Urbagestión – the investment firm that owns the property – has now been forced to allow her to return and pay €533 in rent.  




The eviction prompted the Madrid Tenants’ Union to draw up the Maricarmen decree, which calls for a law against evicting vulnerable individuals without offering them alternative housing. It also proposes curbing unjustified price increases, a freeze on rents and an automatic renewal of leases to prevent unjustified evictions. 




Spain’s Socialist Workers’ party-led coalition government approved the extension of rental contracts, the ban on evicting vulnerable renters and the regulation of seasonal and room rentals that interfere with the supply of affordable housing, although measures must now be approved in congress, where the coalition lacks a majority.




But the government has split its proposal into two decrees

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Stop Helping Saudi Arabia Bomb Yemen, Rights Experts Tell Burnham
content:
Rights experts have urged prime minister Andy Burnham to reverse a decision to refuel Saudi Arabian warplanes as they bomb Yemen.




An open letter to Burnham and foreign secretary Ed Miliband said the UK risks being “complicit in further war crimes” after the government announced last week it would support the Saudi dictatorship’s latest attacks. 




The 

letter is signed by NGOs

 including Shadow World Investigations UK and Campaign Against Arms Trade, as well as eleven human rights and international relations experts. 




It notes the Saudi-led coalition, which the UK first joined in 2015, “stands credibly accused of using starvation as a war tactic” against Yemen and of “widespread attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure.” 




The UN estimates 377,000 were killed in the war on Yemen – which involved 25,000 Saudi-led air raids – between 2015 and 2022, when a ceasefire was announced. 




The new Saudi bombing campaign began after the Houthis seized large areas of land along the Red Sea coast, giving them more leverage over a crucial global shipping route.  




Recent escalation by the Houthis, the letter argues, has been driven by Israel’s UK-backed genocide in Gaza – which saw the Houthis enforce a naval blockade against Israel from 2023 – as well as the illegal US-Israeli war on Iran, a key Houthi ally.

They discuss Andy Burnham’s Labour conference speech, housing, the triple lock, North Sea oil and gas, and how the party is handling debate over the “Zionism is racism” motion ahead of Green party conference.

author: Novara Media
title: Michael Walker Reports From Labour Party Conference 2026
content: Amid the hope, cynicism and confusion surrounding the political direction of Andy Burnham’s Labour party, Michael Walker went to the Labour party conference in Liverpool to find out what’s at the core of the government’s new direction.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Police Broke Teeth and Bones of Students at US Encampments for Gaza
content:
Thousands of pro-Palestine students were arrested on US college campuses, as part of a “widespread, McCarthyite censorship and retaliation campaign”, 

a new report has found

.




Threatened with funding cuts by the Trump administration, colleges and universities across the US played an active role in suppressing pro-Palestinian solidarity, with many students and scholars facing expulsions and deportations.




The report from the American Civil Liberties Union and Amnesty International USA, concludes that universities and law enforcement agencies acted unlawfully during the nationwide crackdown on student-led pro-Palestinian activism.




“Colleges and universities violated basic free speech, association and assembly rights and caused serious harm when they summoned campus police and local law enforcement, resulting in arrests and unlawful and unnecessary use of force,” the report says. 




The report, which spans two years of protests and their aftermath, examined 80 universities across 28 states and Washington DC, and brings together existing research combining documentary evidence with interviews and testimony to identify a broader pattern of repression.




It says universities and law enforcement repeatedly used “heavy-handed and excessive” measures against largely peaceful pro-Palestinian protesters, noting that some students had their teeth and bones broken by police

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Prosecutors Asked to Consider Manslaughter Charges Over Grenfell Fire
content:
Police investigating the Grenfell Tower fire have submitted evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service, paving the way for potential criminal charges.




The Metropolitan Police’s investigation into the fire in North Kensington has identified 54 individuals and 20 companies and organisations. The CPS will now consider whether to move forward with prosecution.




The offences include corporate manslaughter, gross negligence manslaughter, fraud, health and safety offences, as well as misconduct in public office.




The Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC), the council responsible for Grenfell, is among the organisations facing criminal charges.




Almost a decade after the fire, which claimed the lives of 72 people on 14 June 2017, no charges have been brought.




The files submitted today cover all but three of the individuals the Met had said it had identified as being potentially criminally responsible back in 

May.




The CPS has said it is committed to making a decision regarding charges ahead of the 10th anniversary of the fire next year, with trials unlikely to begin before 2029.




As part of its investigation, the police looked into more than 15,000 people and 700 organisations, took 14,700 statements and gathered 165 million electronic files and more than 27,000 physical exhibits.




The Met’s investigation ran alongside the public inquiry, whose final

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: UK Universities Set to Strike in ‘Last-Ditch Fight Over Existential Cuts’
content:
University lecturers are set to walk out over “existential” cuts and course closures, as thousands of students face major disruptions as the new academic year begins.




At least eight universities have announced industrial action for the coming year, including three Russell Group institutions.




At Edinburgh, staff are striking for five weeks to protest £140m of cuts, 1,800 potential job losses and management’s refusal to rule out compulsory redundancies.




The university has also announced that 90 degree programmes will be scrapped from 2027.







The kind of cuts many universities are proposing “will fundamentally reshape higher education in the UK”, Emile Chabal professor of contemporary history at Edinburgh University, told Novara Media. He added there was a risk of university contraction leading to a 

“second deindustrialisation”, given the outsized contribution universities make to local economies.  




Peter Mathieson, Edinburgh University’s principal and vice-chancellor received 

£422,000 in total remuneration in 2023/24

 – equivalent to more than 10 times the university’s 

median staff pay

. As part of his package, 

Mathieson lives rent-free in a university-owned mansion

 on one of Edinburgh’s premier streets, where maintenance costs are also borne by the university.

author: Novara Media
title: Porn Addiction Defines Our Political Age. Here’s How.
content: The effect of pornography on the people who consume it is often moralised about, generally due to its influence over the nascent sexuality of young men. But the business model, technological innovations and broader, parasexual, cultural effects go crucially underexamined. This week’s guest, investigative reporter for the Financial Times, Patricia Nilsson, has written a new book unearthing exactly the ways in which these underexamined forces emerged and how they continue to exert influence on society. She spoke to Ash about pioneering camgirl entrepreneurs, the sado-masochistic-inflected rise of Andrew Tate, and how algorithms have entered the bedroom.

author: Clare Hymer
title: Who Does the Green Party’s ‘Zionism Is Racism’ Motion Really Serve?
content:
It’s Saturday morning in a Victorian public garden in Camden, north London, and the mood is upbeat. Green leader Zack Polanski is fighting a byelection in suboptimal conditions: in a seat with an 11,000 Labour majority, his approval ratings in a slump, and, unlike when the party won Gorton and Denton in February, a prime minister in Downing Street who not everyone totally hates. But on his side he has a party membership surpassing 230,000, of whom around 200 enthusiastic volunteers are out today. If Green members are apparently 

“turning on” Polanski for not being anti-Zionist enough

, as one recent report in the rightwing press claimed, you can’t feel it here. 




But that’s not to say Zionism isn’t being talked about. It is, as much on this sunny morning in Holborn and St Pancras as in the media in recent weeks, because of a controversial motion titled ‘Zionism is Racism’, set to be debated at the party’s conference just days before the 8 October byelection.




The Greens already have strong policies on Israel and Palestine, describing Israeli conduct as apartheid and genocide, backing a full arms embargo, sanctions and an end to occupation and illegal settlements. But the Zionism is Racism motion takes things further. author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: UN’s Israeli Settlements Blacklist Names Firms With UK Public Contracts
content:
Several companies with major British government contracts have once again been named in a 

UN database of firms

 involved in the expansion of illegal Israeli settlements.




The database names 214 companies – 61 more than the previous year – that the UN human rights office has “reasonable grounds to believe” are involved in activities linked to Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.




Earlier this month, the UK government announced new sanctions targeting the settlements, including a ban on the import of goods. 




Foreign secretary Ed Miliband 

said the move

 – which will also involve action against companies that support settlement expansion – was the “beginning of a new approach”.




The firms named in the UN list include French infrastructure giant Egis, which operates the M40 motorway for National Highways; Motorola Solutions, which owns Airwave, the radio network used by British emergency services; and Heidelberg Materials, with which the UK government agreed a major carbon capture deal in 2025. 




Egis was listed for its role in planning the construction of a new light rail network in Jerusalem, which 

rights groups say

 will connect Israeli settlements in occupied East Jerusalem with each other. An Egis spokesperson said the firm “has formally expressed its disagreement with this inclusion” in the UN database.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Pressure Mounts at Labour Conference to Kick Palantir Out of NHS
content:
The NHS’s contract with Palantir has come under pressure at Labour party conference, with 20k party members backing a motion to end the service’s reliance on the US spytech firm. 




Healthcare workers and patients protested outside the venue, calling for the government not to renew a highly controversial £330m patient data contract with Palantir.




The company provides tech to the Israeli military during its genocide in Gaza, as well as custom surveillance tools to ICE in the US.. 




A majority

 of Labour voters

 

(76%) 

 believe Andy Burnham’s government should allow Palantir’s NHS contract to expire without renewal in February 2027.




Around 30 health workers dressed in scrubs attended the No Palantir in the NHS demo outside the conference in Liverpool on Tuesday, ahead of Burnham’s speech. 




NHS doctor Rhiannon Mihranian Osborne, a campaigner at Medact, told Novara Media: “The government has the perfect opportunity to end this contract. It can do so safely and transition over to NHS-owned infrastructure. 




“Palantir’s NHS contract is a threat to the ethics we sign up to as health workers, it’s a 

threat to our patient relationships

 and data privacy, and it’s a threat to the integrity and independence of NHS infrastructure.”

author: Novara Media
title: 130: The Inconvenient Truth About Convenience Culture
content:
Moya and Ash get their nerd on with a conversation about the rise of convenience culture and the loss of enchantment. How can we access feelings of wonder in a world of quick fixes? Is friction the spice of life? (With reference to LOTR, Jaws and Tony Stark.) Plus: when a so-called friend can’t do the bare minimum.




The book Moya mentions is Gabe Bullard’s 

Against Convenience

.




Send us your dilemmas: ifispeak@novaramedia.com


Music by Matt Huxley.

title: Palestine Engulfs the Labour Party Conference

Palestine is topping the agenda of The Labour Party conference with speeches inside and protests out – our correspondents are on the ground to bring you the latest developments.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Ed Miliband Says Brits Outraged Over Palestine ‘Were Right’
content:
Ed Miliband has admitted that millions of Brits outraged by the oppression of Palestinians were “right”, speaking the day after dozens of peaceful pro-Palestine protesters were arrested outside the Labour party conference. 




Miliband used his conference speech in Liverpool on Monday to say to those “moved by the plight of the Palestinian people”: “We hear you. You were right.” His words received loud, sustained applause from the audience.




The foreign secretary is now being called upon by campaigners and former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn to stand up for the rights of people protesting Israel’s ongoing genocide, occupation and apartheid in the Occupied Palestinian Territories and drop the ban on Palestine Action. 




Corbyn told Novara Media that Miliband is “right to vindicate those who spoke up for Palestine” but highlighted that “people are still being arrested for doing exactly that, including people outside the very conference hall in which he made that speech.”




Novara Media 

reported on mass arrests 

of elderly demonstrators outside Labour conference on Sunday, where nearly 200 people had gathered to call on prime minister Andy Burnham to drop the ban on Palestine Action and oppose Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Labour to Nationalise Avanti West Coast Trains After Privatisation Fails
content:
The Avanti West Coast train service will be nationalised in March 2027, Labour has announced, following years of poor service caused by privatisation. 




The service is the latest of numerous lines that have either been brought back into public ownership or will be soon, following a pledge by the ruling party to do so ahead of the 2024 election. 




“Enough is enough. For years, people have been expected to put up with Avanti’s cancellations, delays, overcrowding and a service that has failed them time and time again,” prime minister Andy Burnham 

said in a statement

 on Sunday. 




Re-nationalising the service “means passengers, not shareholders, will come first,” he added. “More investment, fewer delays and a renewed focus on getting the basics right. We’re putting essential services back in public hands and building a railway that actually works for the people who use it.”




Avanti runs services to destinations including London, Manchester, Blackpool, Edinburgh and Birmingham.  




The office of transport secretary Heidi Alexander 

said in a statement

: “From 7 March 2027, taxpayers will no longer be paying fees to a private operator. Instead, every penny will be spent for the benefit of passengers.”




Several operators have been nationalised since 2025, including South Western Railway, Greater Anglia, Govia Thameslink Railway and Chiltern Railways.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Facebook Blocks Lula’s Campaign Ads Just Days Before Brazil Election
content:
Meta briefly disabled ads on the Facebook page of Brazil’s leftwing president on Friday – just days before he faces a far-right challenger in national elections. 




The campaign of incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has filed an appeal with the social media giant and is awaiting an explanation for the incident, state-run 

Agência Brasil reported

.




Lula, 80, is running for a fourth and final term against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of Brazil’s former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro. 




The controversy over the Facebook ads comes after Amnesty International accused Meta of failing to stop the spread of election-related misinformation on the platform. 




The rights group 

ran an experiment in September

 where it submitted 14 ads to Facebook that contained disinformation and “were designed to reflect… tactics that are often used by politicians and candidates to support authoritarian practices.” 




Amnesty’s test ads contained incorrect information on when and where to vote and which candidates were running, Amnesty said, as well as false allegations that “certain candidates were rigging the election”.




Facebook approved eight of the ads containing disinformation. Of the ads it rejected, none were flagged for disinformation. One of the ads that passed said: “We need a military revolution, do not vote in the elections, and the military will take back power if les

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Hope Is Back With Burnham, Apparently – But Not for Pensioners Opposing Genocide
content:
Cast your mind back, for one moment, to January. I was freezing my socks off outside various supermarkets around Manchester, 

chatting to locals

 outraged that then-PM Keir Starmer and Labour’s NEC had blocked Andy Burnham for standing in the Gorton and Denton byelection. 




Fast-forward nine months, and it’s Burnham’s first Labour conference as prime minister under the slogan “Hope again”. How things change. But in other areas, matters are decidedly the same.




Yesterday, we once again saw mass arrests of peaceful protesters under the Terrorism Act, the majority of them elderly pensioners holding paper signs. These scenes were a shameful fixture under Starmer’s government, and now too, it seems, under Burnham’s. 

Undeterred by bouts of wind and rain, 

200-odd people

 gathered outside conference on its opening day to unveil or swiftly pen placards reading: “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action.” 




I’ve reported on a lot of these demos – of varying sizes and in varying kinds of weather – since Palestine Action became the first direct action group in British history to be proscribed as a terror organisation in July 2025 by then-home secretary Yvette Cooper.




What I’m always struck by is the quiet dignity of the older generations – the men and women in their 60s, 70s and above who sit silently with their placards, risking being arrested as terrorists becaus

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Ireland Goalkeeper Boycotts Match Against Israel
content:
Ireland goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu boycotted the squad’s Uefa Nations League fixture against Israel on Sunday to protest the ongoing genocide in Gaza. 




Bazunu took the decision to sit out the game in Hungary after a majority of players reportedly voted to play, despite intense pressure inside Ireland for them to respect 

calls for a sporting boycott

 against the apartheid state. 




“My decision is based purely on my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong,” Bazunu wrote on Instagram. “It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition of the Israeli people or the Jewish community, but against the atrocities in the region.




“There are a few times where you get a chance in life to stand up for something bigger, and I strongly believe that this is one of them.”




The remaining players on the squad did not shake hands with members of Israel’s team or exchange pennants, as part of changes to the pre-match ceremony announced in advance. Ireland beat Israel 3-0. 




Winger James McClean, who has previously played on the Republic of Ireland squad, 

said ahead of the match

 that the team was “forever going to be tarred for not doing the right thing” unless they boycotted.




“I’ve seen some of the interviews saying, ‘We’re uncomfortable with it’ and, ‘It’s not been easy for us,’” he said. “Well then, don’t play the game.”

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Hundreds Defy Palestine Action Ban at Burnham’s First Labour Conference
content:
Almost 200 people gathered outside Andy Burnham’s first Labour party conference as prime minister to defy the ban on Palestine Action by holding signs that read “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action”. 




Two hours into the demonstration on Sunday 27 September – the opening day of the conference in Liverpool – Merseyside police had arrested 15 people under Section 13 of the Terrorism Act.




Those taking part said they were doing so to oppose Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza, to put pressure on Burnham to drop the ban on Palestine Action and to highlight a pressing free speech issue in Britain. 




Protesters, the majority of them retirees, unveiled or penned their signs at 1pm. The demonstration was mostly seated and included British medics, members of the clergy and disabled people with mobility aids. 




Bill, a 71-year-old Church of England priest wearing his red stole and dog collar, told Novara Media: “This is the right place to be, this is where God is.” 




As police started carrying elderly people away, shouts of “well done for arresting pensioners” and “very brave of you to arrest an old man” could be heard. 




Organisers Defend Our Juries said 195 people were taking part in the action.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: Outsourcing Giants Made £6bn in Profit From UK’s Public Services Last Year
content:
Outsourcing companies made an estimated £6bn in profit from public services last year, with close to 11% of all public expenditure going to these private firms.




A new report

 by the think tank Common Wealth found that the public sector spent £129bn on services provided by outsourcing firms, despite the Labour government pledging to bring more public services in-house.




Since the 1980s, private companies have increasingly been brought in to run services once offered by the state. It was hoped that these supposedly efficient firms could break up cumbersome state-owned monopolies. 




But the influx of private companies has just created new monopolies. Serco – which has a £2bn contract with the Royal Navy and also manages 

public bicycle hire schemes

 – gets 90% of its global revenue from public sector contracts, according to Common Wealth’s research. 




Meanwhile, outsourcing giants have faced numerous scandals over the years. Back in 2020 

G4S was fined £44m

 by the Serious Fraud Office after overcharging the Ministry of Justice for tagging offenders, some of whom had died. 




Common Wealth found that around 1.3 million people are employed by these firms in the UK, which is over 

seven times

 the number of police officers in the country. Many of these workers are in low-paid jobs, as the pressure to win public contracts forces wages down, even as their bosses

title: Weapons Firm Gave Advice to UK Universities on Countering Gaza Protests
content:
British weapons manufacturer BAE Systems worked with UK universities to counter campus protests against Israel’s genocide in Gaza, according to emails and internal documents. 




An investigation by 

Liberty Investigates and Al Jazeera

 found 13 UK universities spoke with the firm about how to handle demonstrations. 




In 2024, the company appeared to have urged universities “to counteract an often skewed, but prominent narrative from protesters” about its partnership with higher education institutions, 

slides from a presentation

 show. 




Staff members from one top institution spoke with BAE before disciplining student activists. Another interacted with the company about an upcoming protest against the firm. 




BAE Systems supplies Israel with parts for 

F-35 fighter jets

, which have played a 

key role

 in the Israeli military’s destruction of Gaza.




The 13 universities identified – including Manchester University, Nottingham University, Sheffield University, Southampton University, Birmingham University, Strathclyde and Cranfield – collectively receive as much as £15m via agreements for research funding with the arms manufacturer, according to the investigation. 




Meanwhile, BAE has active “

strategic partnerships

” with Manchester, Strathclyde, Cranfield, Nottingham and Southampton to work on research projects in areas like “AI, quantum mechanics, ma

author: Ash Sarkar
title: Politics Is a Greasy Poll – And For Now, It’s Nigel Farage Who’s Slipping
content:
What will the next general election bring? Though question marks hover over precisely when it will take place, and three years is an aeon in politics, that hasn’t stopped pollsters from trying to predict what the outcome might be. Yesterday 

YouGov dropped an MRP poll

 which showed, if an election were to be held today, Labour would be on course to win largest party, but short of an outright majority. In music to Kemi Badenoch’s ears, the Conservatives would form His Majesty’s opposition, beating Reform into third place. The Liberal Democrats would stay roughly where they are, SNP and Plaid Cymru pick up seats, and the Greens – though gaining a few more MPs – would still not hit double-digits.




Considering that last year’s YouGov MRP showed Labour trailing Reform by more than 150 seats, this is the best news Andy Burnham’s had since Fred Perry opened up its Manchester premises.




Caveats, caveats. Though MRP polls are generally better at predicting election results than ones which presume a unified national swing, there are things they can’t tell you. An MRP can’t take into account how a party might allocate resources and prioritise battlegrounds. It can’t predict future swings in public opinion. And – just to hammer home the point – we’re still really far from the next scheduled general election. Anything could happen. And if the last decade of British politics is anyth

author: Novara Media
title: Reform Tanking in New YouGov Poll
content:
A new Yougov poll predicts that Reform would win fewer seats than Labour and the Tories – with the UK heading for a hung parliament.




Plus: The US and China have agreed to extend their trade war truce, Australia launches an investigation after a medical database was hacked by a rogue OpenAI agent, and Abdul El-Sayed pours cold water on the claims that Israel is not committing a genocide in Gaza.




With Michael Walker, Dalia Gebrial & Elizabeth Ingleson.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: Greta Thunberg Joins Call to Release Hunger-Striking Gaza Flotilla Activists
content:
High-profile political leaders, artists, and activists – including Greta Thunberg – have called for the immediate release of four pro-Palestine organisers who are on hunger strike in a Tunisian jail, including one “on the brink of death”. 




Wael Naouar was rushed to hospital yesterday after spending 40 days on hunger strike, according to the Gaza Sumud Flotilla (GSF), an organisation that looks to challenge Israel’s illegal blockade of Gaza and deliver emergency aid by sea.




Alongside Thunberg, South African politician Zwelivelile Mandela, who is Nelson Mandela’s grandson, has also signed an open letter urging the Tunisian government to free Naouar and his three co-defendants. Both Thunberg and Mandela joined the same aid flotilla as Naouar last year.  




Other 

signatories to the letter

 include Irish rap group Kneecap and Game of Thrones actor Liam Cunningham. They are also calling for “urgent medical care” for the detained men.




The four were arrested in March after being accused of misusing funds raised for the organisation. He launched his hunger strike at Mornaguia prison to protest his detention and that of his fellow activists – Ghassen Henchiri, Ghassen Boughdiri and Nabil Channoufi, who began their strikes around two weeks ago. 




Naouar is in a semi-comatose state, GSF said, adding that the Tunisian authorities have sought to impose an information blac

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Mamdani Forces DoorDash to Pay $131m for Underpaying Workers
content:
Zohran Mamdani has secured a historic $131.5m settlement from food delivery firm DoorDash after it underpaid its workers in New York City. 




The company, which last year 

spent $1.4m

 trying to stop Mamdani from being elected, committed “systematic violations” of the city’s Deliver Worker Laws, the mayor’s office said on Tuesday. 




The violations affected 260,000 workers who were either underpaid, not paid at all, or paid late.   




“This is the largest worker settlement in New York City history and the largest [ever] settlement involving food delivery workers in the United States,” the mayor’s office said.   




Mamdani added: “When a worker earns a wage, they deserve to be paid that wage – not tomorrow, not after a lawsuit, but on time and in full.”




Julie Su, deputy mayor for economic justice, said: “The size of this settlement shows the damage done to workers by wage theft. But it also shows that enforcement matters.”




As part of the settlement, DoorDash will also be monitored under a new system to ensure it remains compliant with the law. 




DoorDash said in a statement that it had underpaid its workers by mistake. “These errors were unintentional, but that doesn’t make them acceptable… We take full responsibility, and we’re deeply sorry.”




The majority of the settlement – $115m – will go directly to delivery workers, while the remaining will go towar

author: Novara Media
title: Iran’s President BLASTS Donald Trump in FIERY UN Speech
content:
More drama at the UN General Assembly as the US delegation storms out of the Iranian President’s defiant speech.




Plus: A former SPAD to Starmer’s government gives us his take on Burnham’s first meeting with Trump, London is running out of kids to teach and can Trump and Xi agree on an AI slow-down deal?




With Michael Walker, Ben Judah, David Krueger & Banseka Kayembe.

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Pro-Palestine Activist ‘Close to Death’ on Hunger Strike in Tunisian Prison
content:
The leader of the Global Sumud Flotilla is in a semi-comatose condition and close to death as he enters the 39th day of his hunger strike inside Tunisia’s Mornaguia Prison, the organisation has confirmed to Novara Media.




Wael Naouar, a father of two who was detained in March alongside three other Flotilla organisers, Ghassan Henchiri, Ghassan Boughdiri and Nabil Chennoufi, initiated his hunger strike in protest of the prolonged detention the Sumud 4 have endured without trial. 




In a press release shared on Tuesday, the Global Sumud Flotilla said Naouar is facing organ failure, and experiencing hallucinations and severe heart, chest and stomach pain. He is described as barely able to see or hear, and “wishes to lose consciousness only to escape the agony”.







After a visit to his son this week, Naouar’s father said: “Wael is on the brink of death.”




Henchiri, Boughdiri and Chennoufi also began their hunger strikes a little over two weeks ago. The Flotilla described Henchiri as “bedridden, in severe pain and denied basic medical care”.




The activists were initially arrested over allegations of financial violations in March. This triggered an investigation into each of the men, and they have remained imprisoned by Tunisian authorities while they await trial. 




A trial date has yet to be set, and their pre-trial detention was 

extended by four months 

on 11 S

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Spain Moves Ahead With US Extradition Case Against Pro-Palestine Millionaire
content:
The Spanish government has allowed an extradition request from the Trump administration to proceed to court, in the first known case of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas.




Defence lawyers for James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, a wealthy donor to leftwing and pro-Palestine causes, say their client is being targeted for his political views. 




Under Spanish law, an extradition request cannot proceed if it is found to be politically motivated.




While the US has yet to publicly outline the full charges against Chambers, his legal team say he is accused of laundering $7.5m (£5.6m) in Tunisia to support Hamas – a charge they strongly deny. 




Chambers’ wife Stella Schnabel, who is Jewish, said the US has failed to provide any evidence for its allegations.




Spain’s national court will now examine the request, with a hearing expected in the coming weeks before the government makes its final decision. Chambers has applied for asylum in Spain, according to his lawyer.




Chambers, a multimillionaire media heir and self-described communist who previously donated to Occupy Wall Street and the Stop Cop City movement, has been held in pre-trial detention in Madrid since his arrest in Ibiza on 10 July.




The decision to allow the case to proceed to the national court is likely to anger members of Spain’s 

leftwing governing coalition

, after they pre

author: Novara Media
title: Trump Gives Wildest Speech yet to UN
content:
Andy Burnham heads to New York for his first face-to-face meeting with Donald Trump, following a filibuster speech to the UN by the US President.

Plus: Former chancellor and now OpenAI employee George Osborne weighs in on the backlash to UK data centres, and Zohran Mamdani delivers a barnstorming speech to a mayoral summit.

With Aaron Bastani & Ash Sarkar.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Tony Blair Wants Governments to Embrace AI, Not Slow It Down
content:
Tony Blair’s think tank has called for governments to embrace AI and rebuild their states around the new technology despite the risks posed to workers, societies and security.




The former Labour prime minister, who has multiple ties to the tech sector, has backed a new paper arguing that countries risk being left behind if they do not adapt to the AI era.




Blair’s vision for AI-powered governance was set out in a 

paper

 released by his think tank, the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (TBI).




“Countries cannot protect themselves from AI by ignoring it,” the paper argues. “The only meaningful path is to engage with it, building institutions capable of operating at the speed and complexity of the world now emerging, and harness AI to transform how the state itself works.” 




The institute’s paper does not make reference to Blair’s own relationship with the tech industry, including the hundreds of millions of dollars in funding his institute has received from tech moguls. 




Larry Ellison, the billionaire founder of software company Oracle, which is heavily invested in infrastructure driving the AI boom, has given 

around £257m in donations and pledges

 to Blair’s think tank since 2021.




In February, campaign group 

Foxglove criticised the UK government

 for collaborating with Blair’s think tank on AI implementation, stating: “Ministers seem to be unabl

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Greta Thunberg Is Taking Sweden to Court Over Climate Crisis Again
content:
Greta Thunberg and Swedish youth climate organisation Aurora are suing the Swedish government over its failures to tackle the climate crisis.




While Sweden has reduced its greenhouse gas emissions at a rate faster than the EU average, the country is 

not on track

 to meet its own target of net zero by 2045.  




Thunberg said on Monday that Aurora has filed a second

 lawsuit

, arguing that Sweden is failing in its legal duty to protect its citizens – especially children and the young – from the effects of climate change.




The group is demanding that Sweden take action to limit global warming to 1.5C by cutting emissions and protecting ecosystems like forests. A third demand involves accounting for emissions that it says are currently excluded from government calculations such as burning imported biomass.




“Sweden, as a rich country with high historical and current emissions, has a legal duty to lead the climate transition,” 

the group wrote in its fundraiser

. “A safe and just world is still possible, but only if rich, high-emitting states like Sweden stop violating their duty to protect people from the devastation of the climate crisis, and start transforming their societies before 2030.” 




Thunberg and Aurora’s first attempt to sue Sweden into taking stronger action against climate change was 

quashed in February

, when the country’s supreme court decreed

author: Novara Media
title: 129: How Did the Pandemic Change You?
content:
What if we still haven’t processed what the pandemic did to us? Was Covid a permanent turning point for our social lives and mental health? Ash and Moya identify an ongoing yearning for connection amid the scare stories and the manic bounceback years. Plus: is it your fault you’re still single?




Send us your dilemmas: ifispeak@novaramedia.com


Music by Matt Huxley.

author: Novara Media
title: German Socialists Win Mamdani-Style Victory in Berlin
content:
Die Linke have won a major election, opening a path to the Berlin mayoralty for Germany’s leftmost party.




Plus: Specialist courts for sexual assault cases are set to be rolled out in England and Wales, fears are rising that war could return to Yemen, and Ed Sheeran has apologised for dropping pro-Palestine rapper Macklemore from his tour.




With Steven Methven, Harriet Williamson, James Jackson & David Wearing.

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Nobel Prize-Winning Economists Back First Billionaire Tax in US
content:
Six Nobel Prize-winning economists have signed an open letter supporting what could be the first billionaire wealth tax in the US, if voters approve it this November. 




The economists, including former chief economist of the World Bank, Joseph Stiglitz, say that a one-time 5% tax on billionaire residents of California could kickstart wealth distribution in the US and across the world. 




Tech entrepreneurs based in and around Silicon Valley have 

spent at least $120m

 lobbying against the tax, known as Proposition 40, since January. Google co-founder Segrey Brin has donated $102m to an opposition group funding an advertising blitz against the ballot. 




In an 

open letter

 published on Saturday, the six economists said the one-off tax could be the first step towards reining in billionaire power. 




“If the state that houses some of the country’s most powerful billionaires votes to tax their wealth, it will kickstart a movement to tax ultra-high-net-worth individuals in other states – and eventually at the federal level and in other countries,” they wrote. 




“As Californians head to the polls, their vote may well come to be seen as a turning point in the battle between democracy and oligarchy.”




They added that billionaires accounted for only 1% of donations during the 2000 federal election cycle, a figure which had jumped to 19% by 2024. 




Alongside Stigli

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Labour Could Win Over 80% of Green and Lib Dem Voters With Progressive Policies, Poll Suggests
content:
Eight in ten Green and Liberal Democrat voters would be open to switching allegiances, depending on Labour’s future choices.




A wealth tax on people worth more than £10 million could convince 37% of respondents who currently support the Greens or Lib Dems to vote for Andy Burnham’s party, according to a new poll carried out for 

Zeteo UK

. 




Where former chancellor Rachel Reeves ruled out a wealth tax under Keir Starmer’s premiership, Andy Burnham has hinted that his government might 

“ask for a little more”

 from rich taxpayers.  The Greens have backed an annual 1% tax on personal wealth of more than £10m – and double that for people with assets of more than £1bn.




Some 36% of respondents to the poll said they would be tempted to vote Labour if the party raised the personal tax-free allowance to £15,000 or higher. Reform UK has also promised to raise this threshold if voted in. 




The polling figures come three weeks before the Holborn and St Pancras byelection triggered by former prime minister Keir Starmer’s resignation as an MP. Green party leader Zack Polanski will stand against Labour’s Camden council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali and Patrick Stillman, the outgoing chair of the Camden Liberal Democrats. 




Other policies that could tempt progressive voters towards Labour include bringing water companies into public ownership, with 31% of Green and Lib Dem voters

author: Simon Childs
title: Labour Rehires Senior Rightwinger Whose Unit Bungled Antisemitism Complaints
content:
A Labour rightwinger who ran the party’s complaints department at the time it bungled numerous antisemitism complaints has been rehired to his previous job.




John Stolliday has been reinstated as head of Labour’s governance and legal unit (GLU) – the body responsible for dealing with complaints.




The role was advertised in the normal way; however, party general secretary Hollie Ridley – 

a close ally of Keir Starmer

 – is understood to have made the appointment in what multiple sources told Novara Media is a factional move before her 

departure from her role

, which will follow the party’s upcoming conference in Liverpool.




In a post on LinkedIn in July, Stolliday said: “Honoured and delighted to have been made executive director of governance and legal at the Labour party – the party I have worked at on and off for over 15 years since I started there in 2004 – and to lead the governance unit which I worked in for so many years.”




Stolliday was director of governance and legal from December 2016 to June 2018, a period in which Jeremy Corbyn was Labour leader and in which the party was mired in antisemitism allegations. The crisis would 

dominate media coverage

 of Labour in the build up to the 2019 election and pave the way for Corbyn’s downfall. 




The crisis culminated in a report by the Equalities and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) which found that Labour

author: Steven Methven
title: How Zohran Mamdani Helped Germany’s Left Party Win in Berlin
content:
In Berlin’s state elections, Germany’s most leftwing party Die Linke has won a significant victory – the biggest in its 

recent

 history. It could also mean that the city gets its first mayor from the party since the fall of the Berlin wall.




That’s partly due to the apparently infinite influence of New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose team helped supercharge the German left with the infectious positivity he’s world famous for. But it’s also down to policy – and in particular a long-standing pledge to expropriate housing from the private sector for public supply in a city where rents have 

soared by 70%

 in the last decade. 




Die Linke’s Elif Eralp, a human rights advocate 

sporting a ‘rent cap’ necklace

, may well become Berlin’s first anti-capitalist mayor since reunification. The daughter of Turkish immigrants, she led the party to a clear victory in Berlin’s Sunday election, taking 26% of the vote – several points over what the polls predicted, by running on a platform squarely targeted at Berliners’ cost of living. 




It all came with a little help from some friends. According to the Washington Post, in the weeks leading up to the race, Die Linke 

sent a delegation to New York

 to meet with advisers to Mamdani. “The success of a democratic socialist in New York, the heartland of capitalism, is a huge achievement,” Eralp 

said last week.

 “We’ve excha

author: Novara Media
title: Nobel Economist Warns: AI Will Destroy Democracy
content:
In the West, liberal democracy, or social democracy, has over the past century become the dominant political system: the water we swim in. But in an age of climate change, runaway inequality, big tech oligopolies, and rising fascism, the system that once promised so much to so many is breaking under the strain. On Downstream this week is Daron Acemoglu, winner of the Nobel Prize in Economics.




His 2012 book ‘Why Nations Fail’ sold over a million copies. This week, he’s here to discuss his latest work, ‘What Happened to Liberal Democracy?’ – a data-packed book that seeks to diagnose and remedy democracy before it’s too late. When and why did liberal democracy stop working for the many? What happened during the transition from an industrial to a post-industrial economy?




How important has the loss of community been? When did progressive politics become overrun by middle-class interests? How does AI further threaten our capacity to self-govern and lead flourishing lives? What could a pro-worker AI look like, and how can we achieve it?

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Hundreds Set to Defy Palestine Action Ban at Labour Party Conference
content:
Hundreds of people will hold signs reading ‘I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action’ outside the first Labour party conference since Andy Burnham came to power, campaigners have said.




The action – planned by Defend Our Juries (DOJ)  for the opening day of the  Liverpool conference on 27 September – is expected to result in mass arrests. 




Since its proscription in July 2025 under Keir Starmer’s leadership, police have arrested more than 3,600 people for showing support for Palestine Action. Officers have carried away hundreds of elderly and disabled people, as well as teachers, doctors and religious leaders.




The upcoming action is intended to put pressure on the new prime minister to depart from Keir Starmer’s policy of denying the genocide in Gaza and treating domestic dissent as terrorism. 




Campaigners note that an increasing number of Palestine Action activists are facing terrorism-related sentencing provisions in British courtrooms, despite not being charged with terrorism offences. 




Four activists from the group were the first to receive increased sentences in reference to a ‘terror connection’ in June. They plan to appeal their sentences, 

Novara Media revealed

 earlier this month. 




In July, the Metropolitan Police 

arrested multiple people

 in proximity to a DOJ rally even though they were not holding signs supporting Palestine Action.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Australia Considers Ban on Meta Glasses in Government Buildings
content:
The Australian government is mulling a ban on Meta glasses in public offices and buildings. 




The proposed restrictions, which would apply to all camera-equipped smart glasses, would be world-leading, prime minister Anthony Albanese’s government said.




It would be the first time a government had prohibited the privacy-invading technology across all of its departments.   




Last month, court officials in England and Wales

 told the Guardian

 that smart glasses had been banned in court buildings. 




Katy Gallagher, Australia’s public services minister, said she was seeking advice on a potential ban. 




“We need clear and consistent guidance for public servants,” she said. “Smart glasses can raise legitimate privacy and security concerns, particularly because of their ability to record and capture information.”




The wearable tech has been branded by some as “pervert glasses”. Women have complained about 

being filmed without their knowledge or consent

 by men expressing romantic interest in them, who then upload the videos to the internet. 




Toluwa Omitowoju told CBS Chicago last month that she had no idea a man had filmed her until her friend started sending her the videos, which had by then reached hundreds of thousands of views. 




More than 70 people in the US are suing Meta, alleging the glasses

 captured intimate images of them

 and shared them with

author: Sophia Sheera
title: US Likely Committed War Crimes in Iran, Say UN Experts
content:
The US likely committed war crimes when it killed at least 178 Iranians in two airstrikes in February, 

a UN fact-finding mission has said

. 




More than 150 people, including 120 children, were killed after two Tomahawk missiles hit a primary school in Minab, southern Iran, on 28 February. On the same day, 22 civilians were killed in a strike on a sports complex in the southern city of Lamerd. 




The mission said on Thursday it believed the US had indiscriminately attacked civilians and damaged civilian infrastructure in both incidents. It said it applied a “reasonable grounds to believe” standard of proof to reach its conclusions. 




The UN experts said that while the Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School was next to an Iranian military naval complex, it was “clearly identifiable” as a school.




“Photographs and videos depicting the school… included child-oriented murals painted on exterior walls, school signage, and playground areas,” they wrote.  




They concluded that “the building of the school was the intended point of impact” for two Tomahawk missiles, adding that the attack was not “an errant strike or collateral damage”. 




They added: “When targeting the school building, the US acted wilfully.” 




The US military initially denied responsibility for the attack before launching its own internal probe in March. The results of that investigation are yet to be

author: Simon Childs
title: Reform MP in Hypocrisy Row After Rightwing Think Tank Flies Him to Italy
content:
A Reform MP who rails against foreign influence in British politics was accused of “absurd hypocrisy” after accepting a trip to Italy paid for by a Dutch think tank.




In July, Danny Kruger took the all-expenses paid trip courtesy of the Center for European Renewal (CER), a pan-European rightwing organisation, based in the Netherlands, which says it is dedicated to “the Western ideal of a civilised, humane and free society”. The CER has ties to the former far-right, authoritarian government of Viktor Orbán, which ruled Hungary from 2010 until he was finally dislodged in an election in April this year.




The Dutch-based organisation spent £724.24 on his flights, hotel and meals over the course of the two-day trip from 8 to 9 July, according to the parliamentary register of members’ financial interests. He claimed the purpose of his visit was to “attend a day-long discussion of global affairs”.




The CER organises an annual meeting called the “Vanenburg conference”, named after the Dutch town in which it was first held. It is unclear whether this is the event Kruger attended – neither Kruger, Reform UK nor CER responded to a request for comment.




Only months before his jaunt to Italy, 

Kruger spoke in the House of Commons

, alleging “glaring foreign interference” in the Gorton and Denton by-election.




In the March 2026 debate on the Representation of the People Bill

author: Ash Sarkar
title: Can’t Persuade Voters? Tom Watson’s New Palantir Job Shows You Can Just Buy Their Democracy
content:
Back in the halcyon days of Corbynism, I spent a lot of time thinking about Tom Watson. The then-deputy leader of the Labour party was 

the right’s man on the inside

; either a noble fighter in service of the moderate cause, or a committed wrecker, who weaponised antisemitism allegations to 

undermine his own party

. He resigned from the post, and stepped down from the House of Commons, just one month before the 2019 general election.




What’s he been up to these days, I hear you ask? Well, six years after being elevated to the House of Lords by Keir Starmer, further congratulations are in order. Watson’s just been appointed as 

Palantir’s newest senior vice-president

, working closely with Louis Mosley (grandson of Oswald, and the second-worst Mitford sister). A hero of the working man, a Labour titan, through and through.




Watson’s new job is more of a promotion than a big move: the Baron of Wyre Forest had been a member of Palantir’s advisory board since 2024. According to the company – named, reassuringly, after the evil and corrupting magic seeing stones from The Lord of the Rings – Watson’s role will be to increase the “social and economic value” of its work through public services, jobs and skills. Translation: this former minister will help grease our way to the government teat.




The assistance of an ex-Westminster big dog couldn’t come a moment too soon f

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Netanyahu Vows to Strip Citizenship From Israelis Who Criticise the IDF
content:
Benjamin Netanyahu is calling for a new law that would strip citizenship from Israelis who criticise the Israeli Defence Forces (IDF).




The proposed law comes in the wake of an Israeli backlash against the directors of NAZA, a documentary about the Israeli military’s AI-assisted mass slaughter of civilians in Gaza which won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival last week.




In a 

video posted on X

 on Wednesday, the Israeli prime minister called for a change in law which would mean “anyone who slanders IDF soldiers” could have their citizenship revoked. 




Netanyahu said: “We will hit them in their pockets and also in their citizenship, because their place is not among us.” He also called for a second new law that would raise “the defamation damages they can be sued for twentyfold.”




Netanyahu’s post, captioned “we will stand by our heroic warriors”, comes after Israeli culture minister 

Miki Zohar wrote to the state’s immigration authorities

 asking for NAZA directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor to be stripped of their citizenship on Monday. 




Netanyahu has 

repeatedly claimed

 that Israel is the “only true democracy in the Middle East”.




Abraham and Szor, who won an Oscar for their debut documentary No Other Land along with two Palestinian directors in 2025, have been subjected to a campaign of escalating threats, including verbal attacks

author: Clare Hymer & Sam Knights
title: Spycops Could Be Authorised to Have Sex With Palestine Action Activists, Says Ex-Special Branch Chief
content:
A former spycop who once led the Metropolitan police’s special branch has said that in some instances undercover officers could be authorised to have sex with Palestine Action activists.




Roger Pearce, head of the controversial counter-terrorism command from 1999 until 2003, told the ongoing ‘spycops’ inquiry that sexual relationships could be authorised as “a means of infiltrating activity involving, for example, a breach of military bases with an intention to inflict serious economic damage on, as we’ve seen recently… [an] aircraft”. 




“I’m contemplating, for example, a breach of a factory making a particular product,” he continued, “to damage equipment in that factory and going equipped with, for example, sledgehammers with which you may injure a police officer.”




These examples appear to refer to two actions carried out by Palestine Action: one in which activists allegedly broke into RAF Brize Norton and spray-painted planes; the other in which a group damaged Israeli military assets at a Bristol factory, with one activist, Samuel Corner, striking an officer with a sledgehammer (Corner was later convicted of grievous bodily harm without intent).




“I’m using existing examples which we have seen reported recently, or fairly recently, as the kinds of things which might justify that authorisation,” Pearce told an inquiry evidence hearing on 15 July. 




Pearce said

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Macklemore Pledges Entire $1m Ed Sheeran Tour Fee to Palestine
content:
US rapper Macklemore has pledged his entire $1m tour earnings to Palestinian relief organisations after being dropped from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour for making pro-Palestine comments onstage.




Macklemore, real name Ben Haggerty, announced the donation days after being removed from the remaining US dates of the tour, following pressure from pro-Israel billionaire and 

AIPAC mega-donor 

Robert Kraft. 




In a 

statement shared on Instagram

 on Wednesday, Mackelmore said: “I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under occupation and still fighting for their freedom.




“I will be donating the entire $1 million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to six organizations working directly to support the Palestinian people.”




He also challenged Kraft to match his donation. 




Kraft issued a statement in response, saying that Sheeran had “called” and “asked me to commit $2m to match his donation to aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis”.







The Kraft Group CEO and New England Patriots owner, worth a reported $13bn, did not specify which organisations would receive the money. 




Macklemore’s $1m 

will be going to

 six Palestinian relief organisations: Palestine Children’s Relief Fund, Anera, HEAL Palestine, Medical Aid for Palestinians, Gaza Soup Kitchen and UNR

author: Joe Sandler Clarke & Harriet Williamson
title: Trump to Send 40k Bombs to Israel in $2.8bn Deal
content:
The Trump administration is planning to send 40,000 powerful bombs – each weighing 2,000lbs (907kg) – to Israel, as part of a vast arms deal worth $2.8bn (£2.1bn).




The package includes 20,000 MK-84 general purpose bombs and 20,000 thermally-coated BLU-117s variants, along with I-2000 Penetrator warheads, 

the Washington Post

 reported on Tuesday.




It is 

reportedly the biggest single 

sale of 2,000lb bombs in recent years. 




MK-84s create an explosion that “sends metal fragments in every direction for thousands of feet, can rip through metal and thick concrete, and often creates large craters in the earth”, according to the Post.




Action on Armed Violence notes that MK-84s can “blow apart buildings and kill and injure people hundreds of metres from the point of detonation”. 




Israel has used 2,000lb bombs 

hundreds of times

 in its attacks on Gaza and Lebanon, including in areas the IDF said were safe for civilians. 




The arms package will be largely paid for through foreign military financing, whereby 

US taxpayers provide money to Israel

 to buy American-made weapons.




Gregory Meeks, a senior democrat on the congressional committee that reviews weapons deals, said he would oppose the sale over concerns that they will not be used by Israel in line with US and international law. 




Meeks 

described the munitions 

as “some of the most destructiv

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: US War Secretary Faces Impeachment Call Over Iran ‘Crimes’
content:
A Republican congressman has 

called for the impeachment

 of US secretary of war Pete Hegseth, accusing him of “high crimes” over the war on Iran. 




Representative Thomas Massie also 

said Hegseth had started

 the war without congressional approval, mishandled top secret intelligence and potentially violated the Geneva Convention.




However, Massie’s attempt to impeach Hegseth – and his bipartisan effort to release more files in the Jeffrey Epstein investigation – are now blocked from being voted on after House speaker Mike Johnson decided on Wednesday 

to close Congress early

.




Johnson said Hegseth has done an “extraordinary job at the Department of War”.




Impeachment in US politics is a process whereby lawmakers accuse public officials of misconduct. On its own, it is not enough to be removed from office – president Donald Trump was 

impeached twice

 in his first term – but it can lead to removal.




Late last year, Hegseth was rebuked for “

endangering military personnel

” after he shared military intelligence in a Signal group chat on his personal phone. 




In March, he told a news conference about the Iran conflict: “We will keep pushing, keep advancing, no quarter, no mercy for our enemies.” Massie noted this phrase could be interpreted as a war crime, as it implies that troops should ignore their opponent’s surrender and 

kill them instead

.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: UK Trade Unions Back Palestinian-Led BDS Movement in Historic Vote
content:
The Trade Union Congress (TUC) has endorsed the Palestinian-led movement for boycotts, divestment and sanctions (BDS), days after foreign secretary Ed Miliband said he “wholeheartedly opposed” the campaign. 




TUC Congress – an annual gathering of the UK’s major unions in Brighton representing over five million workers – voted to support the movement to apply diplomatic, economic and cultural pressure to end Israel’s apartheid policies and other crimes against Palestinians.




The 

motion describes BDS

 as “an effective strategy to pressure Israel to end its ongoing genocide, system of apartheid, occupation and denial of the right of return for refugees”. 




The vote commits the TUC, and its member unions, to actively campaign for the UK to end 

military cooperation

 with Israel and support the introduction of broader sanctions against Israel.




It also commits them to supporting “trade unionists, including artists and culture workers, who refuse to handle goods and services linked to violations of international law.”




Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced sanctions on illegal settlements in the West Bank last week, accusing Israel of turning a “

blind eye to ethnic cleaning

” in the territory. But he stopped short of introducing sanctions on Israel as a whole and said he “wholeheartedly opposed” the BDS movement.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: UK Lawyers for Israel Want Doctors Without Borders Branded a Terror Group
content:
A group of pro-Israel lawyers is urging the UK government to label Doctors Without Borders a terrorist organisation over its work in Gaza. 




UK Lawyers for Israel (UKLFI) allege that the charity – which provides life-saving medical aid to people in warzones – has links to militant groups, and have called on home secretary Shabana Mahmood to proscribe the charity.




If acted on, the move would see the Nobel Peace prize-winning NGO – also known as Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) – categorised the same way as Isis in UK law. It would also make donating to or expressing support for the group a criminal offence. 




Throughout its genocide in Gaza, Israel’s military has 

killed 15 MSF employees

, as well as over 1,000 other humanitarian workers, 

according to the UN

. 




On Monday, MSF said Israel had bombed one of its buses, injuring one of 10 humanitarian workers on board. The bus was clearly marked as an MSF vehicle, the charity said in a statement. 




“Once again, Israeli forces have shown a blatant disregard for the safety of humanitarian and medical personnel. Nowhere is safe in Gaza. Civilians, healthcare workers and humanitarian staff must be protected,” it added.




UKLFI allege links between people working for MSF in Palestine and militant organisations.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: Migrants in US Locked in Tiny Cages That Guards Called ‘Calming Areas’
content:
A notorious detention centre in Florida kept immigrants in cramped metal enclosures that posed “significant risks” to their health and safety, 

a report by a US government

 watchdog has found. 




The cages – which had only 1.6 sq metres of floor space – were referred to by guards at the ‘Alligator Alcatraz’ facility as “calming areas”. 




Detainees were placed inside for periods ranging from a few minutes to a couple of hours, investigators from the Department of Homeland Security’s inspector general’s office found. 




Their report said “the use of such restrictive spaces is highly unconventional and does not align with standards for humane treatment”.




Amnesty International 

found earlier this year

 people held at the South Florida Detention Facility, as it’s officially known, y were “arbitrarily detained” in “unsanitary conditions” where sewage flowed into sleeping areas. 




This month, two guards were arrested following allegations they had 

struck a detainee

. They face misdemeanor battery charges and have pleaded not guilty.




The facility – which got its name when president Donald Trump joked that it was so remote detainees would need to “learn how to outrun an alligator” – was closed in June, despite becoming a focal point of the administration’s anti-refugee policy. 




The previous year, 

a judge ruled

 that the site had to close and no new inmate

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: Supermarkets Sue in Bid to Stop Mamdani’s Plan for Cheaper Groceries
content:
Zohran Mamdani’s plan to create city-run grocery stores to help New Yorkers struggling with the cost of living is being challenged in court by supermarkets, who say they won’t be able to compete with the stores’ low prices.




The New York City mayor plans to create five municipally owned stores on city-owned property by 2029 that will offer a 30% discount on goods like meat, dairy, and fruit and vegetables. 




The lawsuit – led by the National Supermarket Association and supported by other groups and private stores – says Mamdani’s policy would create an unfair business environment. It also alleges that the administration failed to conduct a “serious analysis” of how local business would be impacted by the move.




It follows 

a similar legal action

 launched last month by the Multicultural Business Coalition, which argued Mamdani did not have the legal authority to set up the stores. 




Attorney Mark Jaffe, the coalition’s general counsel, told CNN: “You cannot expect hard-working small business owners to compete with a supermarket that isn’t going to pay rent, won’t have to pay an electric bill and won’t have to buy their products at full price. They cannot possibly compete because no one will be subsidising them.”




Mamdani said last week he remained committed to his plan.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: UK’s Trade Ban on Israeli Settlements ‘Falls Far Short of Legal Obligations’
content:
The UK government has been urged to go further on sanctions against Israeli settlements in the West Bank, with senior lawyers warning that current measures “fall far short” of Britain’s obligations under international law.




Foreign secretary Ed Miliband last week announced a ban on the trade of goods with illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, a move seen as a major shift in UK-Israel relations. Canada and France announced similar actions the same day.




But 130 top lawyers and legal academics have written to prime minister Andy Burnham to say the measures do not meet the UK’s legal obligations, including those set out in a 2024 ruling by the International Court of Justice.




The letter’s signatories include former Lord Justice of Appeal Sir Alan Moses, prominent barrister Michael Mansfield KC and Ralph Wilde, a professor of international law at UCL.




They said they welcomed the new measures but that the UK must now extend sanctions to more sectors of Israel’s economy, prevent public bodies investing in settlements and enforce a full arms embargo.




Miliband last week said the UK would “continue to support important and valued trade” with Israel outside of illegal settlements, adding that he “wholeheartedly” opposed the boycott, divestment and sanctions movement.

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Israeli Minister Threatens Documentary Makers With Citizenship Revocation
content:
An Israeli minister has threatened to have the directors of NAZA – a documentary about the Israeli military’s AI-assisted genocide in Gaza – deprived of their citizenships. 




Culture minister Miki Zohar has written to Israeli immigration authorities, accusing directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor of “treason against the state” and being “willing to harm their homeland just to get applause from antisemites around the world”, he wrote 

in a post on X

.




“Anyone who acts against the state of Israel during wartime cannot continue to hold Israeli citizenship,” he added. 




The move comes after NAZA won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival on Sunday and prompted a record-breaking standing ovation lasting more than 24 minutes. 




The film shows Abraham and Szor as they interview 24 military and intelligence whistleblowers, who together outline Israel’s use of AI-powered systems to target and kill Palestinians in Gaza. 




The interviewees claim that Israeli forces prefer to attack targeted Palestinians in their homes at night, regardless of nearby neighbours or family members. 




The word “NAZA” itself is a Hebrew acronym used by the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) to mean ‘collateral damage’ – or civilian death. In one instance, approval was given to carry out an attack on one Hamas member that would kill 500 civilians.

author: Simon Childs
title: George Galloway to Stand in Byelection in Attempt to Defeat Green Leader
content:
George Galloway has signalled his intention to come out of self-imposed exile in Russia in order to oppose Green leader Zack Polanski in the byelection for Keir Starmer’s former seat.




Polanski was 

selected as the Green candidate

 last week for the byelection, which was triggered when former prime minister Keir Starmer announced he would stand down as an MP. 




Galloway – a perennial byelection candidate – made his announcement on his “Mother of All Talk Shows” programme, in which he also praised Russia’s military prowess after it hit Yahodyn near the Ukraine-Poland border in a drone strike.




The Workers Party of Britain leader said his party would stand “unless the Green party come to the table and make us an offer we can’t refuse,” adding: “If we’re standing, it will almost certainly be me that is the candidate.”




Galloway framed his candidacy as a direct challenge to Polanski. Speaking on his talk show, Galloway cited Polanki’s support for Ukraine and his position on trans rights among the reasons he would oppose him. Later in the show, Galloway said he supports Russia’s war on Ukraine as part of “a wider anti-imperialist, anti-colonialist framework”.

author: Steven Methven
title: Will Reform’s Billionaire Donors Force a Dramatic Burnham U-Turn?
content:
Ching-ching-ching-ching-ching! No, that’s not your alarm clock going off, but the sound of Reform UK hitting the jackpot not once but twice on the billionaire one-armed bandit this weekend. 




The joint £72m gift from two billionaires is made up of £36m from each. And each of those is now the largest ever given in British political history, and almost 

double the campaign funding

 jointly received by Labour or the Tories this year. Talk about bringing a bazooka to a fistfight. But that’s how billionaires roll these days.  




The red flags are raising themselves. We only have to look across the Atlantic to see what happens when big money becomes politics’ piper. The real question is not whether we want billionaires in public life – we don’t –  but why prime minister Andy Burnham backed down when he had the chance to stop it.  




On Friday night, British billionaire and 

Donald Trump-pardonee Ben Delo

 announced he would be giving a £36m donation to Reform UK. By Saturday, that figure had been matched by 

Thailand-based billionaire Christoper Harborne

, he of an earlier 

£5m personal gift

 to Farage, 

the purpose of which

 

nobody has ever

 quite been able 

to get clear

. Harborne’s expressed motivation for the stonking new sum? “My competitive spirit inspired me to match [Delo],” he 

wrote in the Telegraph

.

author: Novara Media
title: The Next Big Shock Is Coming — Green Energy Is the Only Way Out
content:
This summer’s weather has been record breaking in all the wrong ways. Extreme heat, droughts, crop failures, wildfires and thousands of excess deaths have left experts to realise that the climate is destabilising faster than predicted. In the face of this undeniable crisis, what should be done?




Tessa Khan is the founder of Uplift – an organisation that works to challenge the fossil fuel lobby and decarbonise our energy system before it’s too late. The former human rights lawyer realised a decade ago that none of the other social questions matter, if we don’t address the climate crisis. With family in Bangladesh, a nation with 175 million people, that is set to go underwater first, she understands what is at stake better than most. She also understands that Britain is rich in renewables, and the green transition is not just a challenge, but an opportunity to fix our broken economy.




Should Britain drill for more oil in the North Sea, or is this a distraction planted by the fossil fuel lobby? Should the energy system in Britain be nationalised? Are renewables also susceptible to economic shocks? What Can We Learn from the Transition from Oil to Gas? How Does the Ageing Population Impact Climate Politics? And what exactly should Andy Burnham do, on climate change?

author: Novara Media
title: What Did the Situationists Achieve?
content:
In this Trip episode, Nadia, Jem and Keir look back on the antics and manifestos of the socialist revolutionaries who gathered under the banner of the Situationist International.




The ACFM gang chart the SI’s influence on politics and media theory, from the central concept of the Spectacle during the ’68 uprisings to their lingering influence on pop music, psychogeography and political organising. Featuring ideas from Guy Debord, Mustapha Khayati and Raoul Vaneigem and music from the KLF, Sex Pistols and Negativland.
