author: Clare Hymer & Charlotte Reck
title: Police Raid Home of 84-Year-Old Priest Who Joined Just Stop Oil Protest
content:
Police raided the home of an 84-year-old priest following her arrest last week at a Just Stop Oil protest.




Sue Parfitt had been arrested alongside other protesters at Parliament Square in London on Wednesday 2 September during Andy Burnham’s first PMQs, with activists calling on the prime minister 

not to approve new oil and gas licenses

.




Parfitt’s home in Henbury, Bristol, was searched sometime between 7.30pm that evening and noon the following day while she was being held in police custody. 




She only discovered her home had been the site of a swoop when she returned on Thursday afternoon following her release. 




She recalled being told what had happened by her landlord. “I was quite surprised,” she said, “and then I was terrified.” 




It hasn’t been made clear to Parfitt why the raid occurred, although she suspects the police had intended to seize her laptop. 




Parfitt doesn’t have a smartphone or social media. “They [the police] think you’ve got all these contacts on your devices,” she said. “Well, I don’t because I’m not in any of these chats.” 




Parfitt shares her home with her landlord and another tenant, who was not home at the time of the incident. 




No other protesters held in custody last week are believed to have had their homes raided.




Novara Media has approached the police for comment.




Parfitt has been arrested more than 30 time

author: Charlotte Reck, Charlotte England & Clare Hymer
title: Greens Pick Zack Polanski to Stand in Byelection
content:
Zack Polanski will stand as the Green party candidate in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection slated for 8 October, the party confirmed on Friday. 




The announcement means local members voted to select Polanski over a surprise opponent, who ran against him from within his own party. 




Green councillor Hamza Chowdhury announced on Monday that he was also seeking nomination, arguing that as a Camden resident he would be better placed to represent constituents than the party leader, who lives in east London.  




Polanski’s selection comes just ten days after former prime minister Keir Starmer announced his resignation as MP and subsequent departure from the seat. The decision means that, a year on from becoming the Green leader, Polanski could be only weeks away from being catapulted into the House of Commons. 




But first he must face a high stakes contest against Labour – which won the seat with a more than 11,000 majority at the last general election – with the vote due to take place just a week after many Greens decamp to Brighton for the party’s annual conference.




“The Greens might be the underdog in this election, but we have the momentum and we can win,” Polanski told a meeting to announce the party’s candidate on Friday.

author: Charlotte Reck
title: British Adults Overwhelmingly Support UK Ban on Illegal Israeli Settler Imports
content:
A significant majority of British adults support the UK government’s ban on imported goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, a YouGov survey has revealed. 




The survey came on Wednesday, the day after Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced plans to slap sanctions on Israeli goods produced on settler-populated Palestinian land because of the illegal nature of the settlements. 




This is the first time the British government has aligned with a 2024 ruling by the International Court of Justice deeming the occupation unlawful. 




More than half – 52% – of 4,506 people polled approved of the ban, giving credence to an assumption Miliband made in his statement: “I do not believe that the British people want us supporting the occupation by accepting products from settlements in our shops and supermarkets,” he had ventured. 




A breakdown showed 33% “completely” approved of the crackdown on illegal Israeli goods appearing on UK supermarket shelves, and a further 19% “somewhat” approved. 




10% of adults polled indicated they “completely” disapproved with the move, while 7% “somewhat” disapproved with the legislation, forecast to be in place within six to nine months.




Around a third of respondents – 31% – said they did not know how they felt.
